close_reason: Implemented in commit 8d8b6c5. metadata_get now takes 'params: Option<MetadataGetParams>' as the 3rd positional arg, mirroring canonical email_get. Future draft-defined method-level args land as typed fields on MetadataGetParams without breaking the metadata_get signature.
description:
src/methods/metadata.rs:27-51 — metadata_get(ids, properties) ships with two positional args. The canonical sibling email_get takes (ids, properties, params: Option<EmailGetParams>) at mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:27-64. metadata_get has no third params slot.

Once 0.1.0 ships, adding a 'params: Option<MetadataGetParams>' positional arg is a breaking signature change. Every downstream caller breaks at the call site. The fix would be to (a) cut a major version, or (b) add an _ext variant with the new arg shape and deprecate the old, which fragments the API.

The trigger: a future draft revision adds a metadata-specific method-level arg on Metadata/get (e.g. an inline-fetch-children flag, a max-depth, anything). Or the workspace decides to thread vendor extras through every builder (wzq9.2 already covers /set; same logic applies to /get).

Two ways to derisk before 0.1.0:
1. Add 'params: Option<MetadataGetParams>' now with the struct empty-but-for-extras, mirroring how mail-client already exposes EmailGetParams.
2. Replace positional args with a builder. Higher migration cost for cookie-cutter consistency.

Recommendation: (1). Cheap to land now, breaking to land later. Same fix the wzq9.2 bead proposes for /set; this issue extends it to /get for the same reason.
title: metadata_get: no params slot — adding one later is a breaking signature change
